Inspected classification, arithmetic, provenance, stale-history, malformed-count, and recommend-only assertions; the tested expectations are reproducible from their fixtures.
Test-only code is not shipped on an application or ingest hot path.
The detector reads normalized workflow records and emits text only; it performs no auth, egress, command execution, filesystem writes, or client rendering.
Failed-agent token arithmetic accepts negative finite token values as complete accounting, allowing understated evidence and provenance.
Inspected per-run/agent scans, bounded text previews, capped timezone cache and evidence, and burst sorting; no release-blocking hot-path amplification or unbounded retained data was found.
Test-only fixtures do not enforce permissions or execute the generated recommendation snippet.
The tests cover conservative tool-wide, Bash-prefix-boundary, literal, non-Bash, malformed-entry, count, evidence, and fix-output behavior.
Test-only code is not shipped on a request or ingest hot path.
Inspected permission-rule handling: non-string inputs are ignored and findings depend on the conservative shared shadow predicate rather than executing rule content.
Each recommendation is derived from a concrete allow/deny pair, counts each shadowed allow once, cites both rules, and serializes the identified entries without interpolation into executable code.
The nested allow/deny comparison is limited to the small live permission lists and stops after the first covering deny per allow; no material hotspot was found.
Test fixtures contain inert paths and identifiers and do not implement or execute the production command-removal path.
The tests verify family scoping, counts, provenance date, short-window demotion, threshold behavior, and attribution-backed use.
Test-only code is not shipped on a request or ingest hot path.
Inspected the generated removal-command boundary and its directly related builder: untrusted identifiers use JSON encoding and removal paths use shell quoting with option termination.
Unused-resource claims cite computeConfigHygiene fields, restrict evidence to zero-window MCP/plugin findings, attach as-of provenance, and demote short history to provisional/stale.
The detector computes hygiene once, uses linear filtering/counting, and caps visible evidence at five; no material additional ingest latency or retained-memory issue was found.

findings.title: Negative token counts corrupt failed-agent accounting
findings.what: The sum treats every non-null token value as valid and marks only null values unknown. A finite negative artifact value therefore subtracts from the total while still allowing provenance to call the failed-agent counts complete. For example, failed agents with 50000, -20000, and 20000 tokens produce a '~50k' complete claim rather than rejecting the negative row and reporting at least ~70k with one unknown/invalid count.
findings.fix: Accept tokens only when they are finite, non-negative safe numbers; sum only accepted values and include invalid values in the unknown/incomplete count.
findings.acceptance: Add a detector test with three qualifying failures whose tokens are 50000, -20000, and 20000. The recommendation must report at least ~70k known tokens, identify one unavailable/invalid token count, and must not describe the token accounting as complete.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarially re-read the cited reduction, completeness branch, and provenance emission. The directly related baseline parser rejects non-finite values but accepts finite negative numbers, so the malformed value reaches this detector; existing malformed-agentCount defenses do not cover tokens.
